title: Synthesising Audio Adversarial Examples for Automatic Speech Recognition

problem.claim: Well-trained automatic speech recognition models can be fooled into transcribing naturally sounded human audio incorrectly.

gap.claim: Existing audio adversarial examples are typically generated by adding constrained perturbations to benign audio, creating an audio-dependent assumption.

contributions.claim: The Speech Synthesising based Attack constructs audio adversarial examples entirely from scratch without depending on existing audio.
A conditional variational auto-encoder is introduced as the speech synthesiser.
The adversarial audio synthesis task is addressed using a proposed adaptive sign-gradient descent algorithm.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that SSA is proposed for the first time as a novel threat model for constructing audio adversarial examples entirely from scratch.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on Audio Mnist, Common Voice, and Librispeech reportedly show that the method can synthesise naturally sounded audio adversarial examples that mislead state-of-the-art ASR models.
The authors provide a webpage containing generated audio demonstrations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Naturally sounded adversarial audio can cause well-trained ASR models to transcribe incorrectly.
Existing attacks usually rely on constrained perturbations of benign audio and therefore assume access to audio.
SSA is proposed as a from-scratch audio adversarial example generation threat model.
The approach combines a CVAE speech synthesiser with adaptive sign gradient descent.
Experiments across three datasets and an audio-demo webpage are presented as support for the approach.

source_observation.claim: The proposed attack generates adversarial audio entirely from scratch rather than perturbing existing audio.

interpretation.claim: Removing dependence on a benign input can broaden the threat model for adversarial-example generation.

application.claim: When designing robustness evaluations, include attacks that synthesize inputs without access to benign examples when the threat model permits it.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the from-scratch threat model compares with perturbation-based attacks under specific operational constraints.

unknowns: Attack success rates, audio quality metrics, and comparison results are not provided.
The targeted ASR models, experimental settings, dataset sizes, and synthesis constraints are not specified.
The abstract does not provide implementation details sufficient to assess reproducibility.
